sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: headlight triggers, wet and icy stopping distances, hydroplaning, flood depths, fog and wildlife
Confusable pairs among the work zone, night, rain, flood, fog, snow and wildlife rules, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in trailing lines.

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A01
A work zone begins at the first work zone sign and ends at the last one, and an extra speeding penalty applies only when a sign at the start lists it. [A01]
Why it matters: group work zones; difficulty medium; confusable zone limits versus penalty sign.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A02
Headlights are required from sunset to sunrise and also whenever visibility drops to 400 feet or less, even in daytime. [A02]
Why it matters: group headlight law; difficulty high; confusable time trigger versus visibility trigger.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A02
Flash your high beams once to remind an oncoming driver to dim, but if they do not, keep your own lights on low rather than switching to high beams. [A02]
Why it matters: group night driving; difficulty medium; misconception target.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A03
Wet pavement can stretch stopping distance from 2 to 10 times, which is why the following gap should be at least doubled. [A03]
Why it matters: group rain; difficulty high; confusable stopping multiplier versus following multiplier.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A03
Hydroplaning can start at about 30 mph in water just over 1/8 inch deep, and the response is to ease off the gas without braking. [A03]
Why it matters: group hydroplaning; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A03
Cruise control stays off not only while it rains but also after the rain, since releasing it during a hydroplane costs time you may not have. [A03]
Why it matters: group rain equipment; difficulty medium; confusable during versus after rain.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A04
About 6 inches of fast water can sweep a car off the road, while about 12 inches can float or overturn it. [A04]
Why it matters: group floods; difficulty high; confusable sweep depth versus float depth.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A04
In thick fog you pull far off and exit on the passenger side, while in drivable fog you use low beams and watch for the taillights ahead. [A04]
Why it matters: group fog; difficulty medium; confusable stop-and-exit versus drive-carefully.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A04
On snow or ice allow at least 3 times the normal stopping distance, and to stop you lift off the brake and let the engine do the slowing. [A04]
Why it matters: group winter driving; difficulty high; confusable brake pedal versus engine braking.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A05
Use high beams only with no oncoming traffic and no animal directly ahead, because bright beams can freeze some animals in the road. [A05]
Why it matters: group wildlife; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0076]
